An Increase in

Investment An increase
in the demand for investment goods shifts the
investment schedule to the
right. At any given interest
rate, the amount of investment is greater. The equilibrium moves from point
A to point B. Because the
amount of saving is fixed,
the increase in investment
demand raises the interest rate while leaving the
equilibrium amount of
investment unchanged.
